documents.application_scenario: Used to initialize a Parser object from a memory buffer before subsequent parsing operations such as parser_next.
documents.functionality: Initializes a Parser from an in-memory buffer. If size is zero, returns -1 without modifying the parser. Otherwise, sets parser->state to the first byte of data and returns 0.
notes: Only the first byte of data is used to initialize parser->state.
The Parser struct is expected to have a state field.
Related functions include parser_next, node_process, and parser_free.
parameter_notes: parser: non-const pointer to a Parser struct; written to via parser->state.
data: const pointer to the input byte buffer; only data[0] is read when size > 0.
size: number of bytes in data; must be > 0 for successful initialization.
resource_lifecycle_notes: Does not allocate or free memory.
Caller is responsible for the lifetime of the Parser and data buffer.
Parser should be released via parser_free when no longer needed.
documents.signature: int parser_from_memory( Parser *parser, const unsigned char *data, unsigned long size);

documents.application_scenario: Used as a parser-related processing function (PRF) to obtain the next Node from a Parser, typically after the Parser has been created via parser_from_memory and before the Node is passed to node_process.
documents.functionality: Reads the current state field from the given Parser and returns it wrapped in a Node whose value is set to that state.
notes: The function does not advance or mutate parser->state; it only copies the current state into the returned Node.
Related functions include parser_from_memory (ISF/HPF), node_process (PRF), and parser_free (HPF).
parameter_notes: parser is a non-const pointer to a Parser struct; the function only reads parser->state and does not modify the Parser.
resource_lifecycle_notes: The returned Node is a value type; no heap allocation is performed by this function.
The Parser must remain valid for the duration of the call; ownership/lifetime of the Parser is managed elsewhere (e.g., parser_from_memory / parser_free).

documents.application_scenario: Used as a processing step on a Node produced by parser_next, likely to advance or count a value stored in the node during parsing.
documents.functionality: Increments the integer field 'value' of the Node structure pointed to by 'node' by one.
notes: The function assumes node is non-NULL; no null check is present in the source.
Only the 'value' field of Node is accessed.
parameter_notes: 'node' is a non-const pointer to a Node structure; it must point to a valid, writable Node instance.
The function reads and writes node->value.
resource_lifecycle_notes: No allocation or deallocation is performed; the caller retains ownership of the Node.
The Node must remain valid for the duration of the call.

documents.application_scenario: Intended to be called when a Parser instance is no longer needed, as the HPF (heap/parser free) role in the parser lifecycle alongside parser_from_memory (ISF/HPF) and parser_next (PRF). In the current implementation it has no observable effect.
documents.functionality: No-op function body: it explicitly casts the parser parameter to void and performs no reads, writes, or deallocation. It exists as a placeholder or stub for a parser cleanup/free routine.
notes: The (void)parser cast is the only statement, indicating an intentionally empty stub.
Structures referenced in context: Parser and Node.
parameter_notes: parser is a non-const pointer to a Parser struct-like type.
The function body does not read from or write to the pointed-to object; the parameter is cast to void.
A NULL or dangling pointer would be equally safe here since the pointer is never dereferenced.
resource_lifecycle_notes: Despite the name, this function does not free, release, or otherwise modify any resource in the supplied source.
No deallocation or cleanup of the Parser or its associated Node structures is performed.
Callers relying on this function to release memory would leak resources under the current implementation.
